mutants.description: The capture gate is held open while UVLO is asserted, so the brown-out that stops the converter is sure to be recorded. The side effect is that every routine power-down is logged as a UVLO episode.
mutants.reason: On a normal power-down the converter is already stopped when UVLO asserts. The mutant then sets fault_reg[UVLO] and latches fault_time, and the bit sets again after every host read while Vin stays low. The correct design leaves both at zero.

mutants.description: fault_time is cleared all through soft start, as if each restart opened a new episode, while fault_reg keeps its record until the host reads it
mutants.reason: Suppose a record from an earlier episode has not been read when the converter restarts: its fault_time drops to 0 during S_SS. A first cause captured during soft start is also left with fault_time 0, because the stamp is cleared and no new episode starts afterwards.

mutants.description: OVP is inferred only into an empty record, on the belief that an analog latch trip after any other recorded cause must be a consequence of that cause
mutants.reason: Example: an OTP or soft-start overcurrent is recorded and not yet read, the converter restarts, and then the analog OVP trips the latch while it is running. fault_reg[OVP] never sets, so the shutdown cause is missing from the record.

mutants.description: A host read clears fault_reg only while the converter is running, so the cause of a shutdown cannot be read away until the converter restarts
mutants.reason: After the converter has stopped, firmware's normal read returns the record, but fault_reg keeps its bits instead of clearing. fault_time is cleared by the same read, so a non-empty record is left with fault_time 0.
